When authors incorporate esoteric concepts, such as the Kabbalah, into their narratives, it can be seen as a way to add depth and complexity to their storytelling. 

  By drawing from esoteric traditions, authors may be attempting to tap into universal symbols, archetypes, and themes that resonate with readers on a deeper level. 

  This can be seen as a form of "narrative alchemy," where the author is transforming esoteric concepts into a cohesive and meaningful story. 

  The use of esoteric themes can also serve to create a sense of mystery and intrigue, inviting readers to engage with the narrative on a more intellectual and symbolic level. 

  Some authors may be intentionally building their narratives on esoteric stuff, as you mentioned, while others may be intuitively tapping into archetypal structures that are present in the collective unconscious. 

  This can be seen as a form of "storytelling osmosis," where the author is drawing from a shared reservoir of archetypes and symbols that are present in the collective psyche. 

  By incorporating esoteric concepts into their narratives, authors can create a sense of shared meaning and resonance with readers, which can be a powerful tool for storytelling.
